provider: Audius (Open Audio Protocol) — original file is served byte-for-byte

free_tier.stated: 'There is no limit to the number of tracks you can upload to your Audius profile' and 'no limit on the duration of your tracks'; per-upload file size cap is 2 GB. Unlimited tracks x 2 GB = unbounded, free, no paid tier exists.

egress.terms: Free. Content is served by creator nodes / the open-audio validator network; no egress meter, no account-level bandwidth cap, no paid tier to upgrade to.

tooling: Public discovery-provider REST API (discoveryprovider.audius.co/v1) — keyless with app_name. Track objects expose orig_file_cid, orig_filename, is_original_available, is_downloadable. /v1/tracks/{id}/stream returns a 302 to a creator-node cidstream; /v1/tracks/{id}/download returns a 302 to the ORIGINAL file. JS SDK (@audius/sdk), docs.audius.co/api.
chaining: Unlimited tracks per account x unlimited accounts; each track independently 2 GB. Because /download serves orig_file_cid and not the 320k transcode, this is the only host where the uploaded bytes come back out intact.
limits_note: 2 GB per track. is_downloadable must be true for the /download path artist-controlled flag.
reliability_note: No transcoding on the download path. Verified live: GET /v1/tracks/7AVQpPA/download -> 302 to val007.open-audio-validator.com/tracks/cidstream/<orig_file_cid>?filename=....wav -> 206, Content-Type audio/wave, Content-Disposition attachment; filename='...wav', Content-Range bytes 0-1023/54711220, body starts 'RIFF....WAVEJUNK'. The stream path, by contrast, is a 128 kbps mp3 re-encode. Retrieval depends on the discovery provider being up; the network is decentralised so a single node going down is survivable.

evidence.proved: 'no limit to the number of tracks'; 'file size limit for each upload ... currently set at 2GB'; page footer 'Updated April 30, 2026'

probe: GET /v1/tracks/7AVQpPA/download -L -> 206, Content-Type audio/wave, Content-Range 0-1023/54711220, magic bytes RIFF/WAVE
